patients.summary: 70-year-old retired retail supervisor with hypertension, type 2 diabetes, hyperlipidemia, obesity and ongoing heavy smoking, who develops glaucoma, nodal osteoarthritis, postherpetic neuralgia and, after her last practice visit, a psychiatry diagnosis of Alzheimer disease.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT VISIT

62 y/o woman transferring care; her longtime PCP is retiring. Retired from retail (store supervisor, 20+ yrs on her feet). Here alone.

Problems she brings:
- HTN x ~9 yrs, on HCTZ 25 daily. Checks BP at the pharmacy machine now and then, "usually in the 120s."
- T2DM dx ~2011, metformin 1000 BID. Last A1c she remembers was "around 7." No hypoglycemia (not on anything that would cause it). Mild GI upset when she started metformin, long gone.
- Hyperlipidemia on atorvastatin 40 since the diabetes dx. No myalgias.
- Weight: has been heavy since her 40s. Tried a commercial program twice.
- Smoker: 1 ppd since about age 30, so ~32 pack-years. Has cut down before but never quit for more than a few weeks. Not interested in a plan today.

PSH: hysterectomy at 48, lap chole at 52. No complications.
FHx: mother has late-onset Alzheimer's (dx at 78). Father had T2DM, HTN, high cholesterol, died of an MI at 72. Maternal grandmother had glaucoma. Sister has osteoarthritis.
SHx: divorced, one grown daughter nearby. No alcohol. No drugs.
Meds: HCTZ 25 qAM, metformin 1000 BID, atorvastatin 40 qHS.
Allergies: NKDA

ROS: no chest pain, dyspnea, claudication, polyuria, numbness in feet, vision change, GI or GU complaints.

Exam: vitals as charted, BMI 33. Pleasant, NAD. Fundi not well seen undilated. Neck supple, no thyromegaly, no bruits. RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear, no wheeze. Abd obese, soft, well-healed lap scars. No edema. Feet: skin intact, no calluses, pulses 2+ DP/PT, monofilament intact bilaterally.

A/P
1. HTN - at goal on HCTZ. CMP today.
2. T2DM - A1c, UACR, lipids drawn this morning. Continue metformin. Wants an eye exam this year with her usual optometrist.
3. HLD - continue atorvastatin 40.
4. Obesity BMI 33 - talked about walking; she's open to it.
5. Tobacco use - advised to quit, gave quitline number. Lung screening to discuss next visit when she's had time to think.
6. HM - HCV and HIV screening once (agreed). Mammogram ordered. Records request for colonoscopy date. Flu shot next month when we get stock.
RTC 6 months, sooner prn.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Dorothy, your labs from Tuesday are back. A1c just under 7 -- right where we'd hope for you. Kidney function, potassium and liver tests normal. Cholesterol well controlled on the atorvastatin. Urine protein normal. Blood counts normal. Hepatitis C and HIV screens negative. No changes. See you in March, and please do the mammogram when you can.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care office
documents.author: MA
documents.body:
Records received from her previous internist (34 pages), abstracted:
- Colonoscopy 2016: normal to the cecum, no polyps; repeat in 10 yrs (2026).
- Screening mammogram 2017: negative, BI-RADS 1.
- Diabetic eye exam (optometry) 03/2018: no diabetic retinopathy.
- Pneumococcal and shingles vaccines: none recorded. Last tetanus 2008 (Td).
- Med list matches ours: HCTZ 25, metformin 1000 BID, atorvastatin 40.
Routed to PCP. Original filed under Media.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Flu Vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Here for flu shot. No fever today, no prior reaction. Quadrivalent 0.5 mL IM left deltoid, lot recorded. VIS given. Tolerated well, waited 15 min. Reminded about mammogram -- she's scheduled 11/7.

reports.text: Bilateral screening mammogram with tomosynthesis. Comparison: 2017 outside study. The breasts are scattered fibroglandular density. No suspicious mass, calcification or architectural distortion in either breast. No change from prior.
reports.conclusion: Negative. BI-RADS 1. Routine screening mammogram recommended.

documents.title: Screening Mammogram
documents.author: radiology
documents.body: Screening mammogram 11/7/2018: negative, BI-RADS 1. Letter mailed to patient by imaging center. Reviewed -- PCP.

documents.title: Refill request
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pharmacy requests metformin 1000 mg #180 for 90-day supply (insurance prefers mail-order quantity). Last A1c in Sept at goal, visit due March. Approved per protocol, 1 refill.

documents.title: Follow-up: DM, HTN
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: 6 mo f/u. Walking the mall with her sister 3 mornings a week through the winter. Still smoking a pack a day. No CP/SOB. No missed doses. Some heartburn after big meals, rare.
Meds: HCTZ 25, metformin 1000 BID, atorvastatin 40. NKDA.
O: BP and weight as charted -- weight about the same. Heart regular, lungs clear, no edema. Feet: intact sensation, good pulses.
A1c sent today.
A/P:
- T2DM: A1c pending; has been at goal. Continue metformin.
- HTN: controlled. BMP today.
- Tobacco: talked again; not ready. Shared decision on lung cancer screening: she qualifies by age and pack-years; discussed false positives and radiation. She'd like to do it. LDCT ordered.
- Due for eye exam -- she'll call her optometrist.
RTC Sept for physical.

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text: Baseline low-dose CT of the chest without contrast. Lungs: no pulmonary nodules. No consolidation or effusion. Airways patent. Mediastinum and hila unremarkable; no adenopathy. Heart normal in size. Visualized upper abdomen unremarkable; cholecystectomy clips.
reports.conclusion: Lung-RADS 1: negative. Continue annual screening in 12 months.

documents.title: LDCT Lung Screening
documents.author: radiology
documents.body: Baseline lung screening CT: Lung-RADS 1, no nodules. Repeat 12 months. Pt notified through portal.

documents.title: Diabetic eye examination
documents.author: optometry
documents.body:
EYE EXAMINATION REPORT -- diabetic patient
Exam date 06/14/2019. Dilated fundus exam both eyes.
Best corrected VA 20/25 OD, 20/25 OS. IOP 17/18 (applanation).
Lens: early nuclear changes OU, not visually significant. Optic nerves pink with healthy rims OU. Macula flat, no hemorrhages, exudates or microaneurysms. Periphery intact.
Impression: Type 2 diabetes without retinopathy. Mild refractive change; new glasses Rx given.
Return 12 months.

documents.title: Eye exam
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Had my eye exam, they said no diabetes damage. They were going to fax you. Also new glasses, finally!

documents.title: RE: Eye exam
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Thanks Dorothy -- we got the report and it's in your chart.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ANNUAL EXAM
63F. Feels fine. Walking less since the summer heat. Still smoking 1 ppd.
Diet: trying to skip the afternoon soda.
Screening: colonoscopy 2016 normal (next 2026). Mammogram 11/2018 negative. LDCT 5/2019 Lung-RADS 1. Eye exam June -- no retinopathy. S/p hysterectomy, no cervical screening needed. HCV/HIV done.
Meds unchanged. NKDA.
ROS negative x 12 systems.
Exam: well-appearing. HEENT normal. Neck no nodes/thyromegaly. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Ext no edema. Skin no worrisome lesions. Feet: monofilament normal, pulses good. PHQ-2 0.
A/P:
- Preventive: Tdap today (last tetanus 2008). Flu today. Shingrix discussed -- she'd rather wait, says her arm got sore with the last tetanus. Fasting labs drawn.
- DM/HTN/HLD stable; labs pending.
- Smoking: counseled. Not ready.
F/u 6 mo.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your physical labs all look good: A1c holding near 7, cholesterol at goal, kidneys and liver fine, no protein in the urine, normal blood count. Keep walking! Next visit in the spring.

documents.title: Refill
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, the pharmacy says my atorvastatin has no refills left. Can you send it? I have 4 pills. Thank you, Dorothy

documents.title: RE: Refill
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Sent atorvastatin 40 mg, 90 days with 3 refills, to your usual pharmacy. Should be ready by noon. -RN
